---
title: "User guide"
guide-section: "Getting Started"
---

The sidebar splits the work into two steps: find a player, then load
their stats. Each step has its own button.

## 1. Tell the app what kind of player you want

Three controls at the top of the sidebar set the search scope and the
metric list:

| Control       | Choices                                      | What it does                                                                          |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Player type** | *Active players*, *Retired players*        | Sets how far back the player search reaches. *Active* uses a small 3-season window for instant typeahead; *Retired* widens to ~50 seasons so older retirees come up. |
| **Position**  | *Batter*, *Pitcher*                          | Swaps the metric list and the weight column used in the curve fit (PA for batters, IP for pitchers).                                                                  |
| **Metric**    | Batter or pitcher rate stats (see the list below) | Which stat to plot. Each dropdown option spells the acronym out, and a one-line definition appears below the dropdown when you change it. Full definitions, formulas, and benchmarks live on the [Metrics](03-metrics.qmd) page. |

The Metric choices change with **Position**:

| Position | Available metrics |
| -------- | ----------------- |
| **Batter**  | **OPS** (on-base + slugging), **OBP** (on-base percentage), **SLG** (slugging percentage), **AVG** (batting average), **HR** (home runs), **ISO** (isolated power; `SLG − AVG`) |
| **Pitcher** | **ERA** (earned run average; lower is better), **WHIP** (walks + hits per inning pitched; lower is better), **K/9** (strikeouts per 9 innings), **BB/9** (walks per 9 innings; lower is better), **HR/9** (home runs per 9 innings; lower is better) |

![The sidebar with the defaults: Active players, Batter, OPS. The inline help line under the Metric dropdown shows the formula and benchmark for the selected stat.](images/sidebar-active-batter.png){width=320px fig-alt="Sidebar configured for an active batter"}

## 2. Find a player

Type a name in the **Player name** box (≥2 characters). As you type,
the dropdown below fills with matches. Each row shows the player's
name, primary position, and debut–final seasons:

```
Mike Trout — CF (2011–Active)
Steve Trout — P (1978–1989)
```

The position tag (`CF`, `P`, etc.) lets you confirm at a glance that
the player's position matches the **Position** toggle on the left.

### The dropdown is filtered by Position

The dropdown filters matches by primary position, so you can't pick a
position player while *Pitcher* is selected (or vice versa):

| Position toggle | What you see in the dropdown                                 |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Batter**      | Every primary position except pure pitchers (`P`). Catchers, infielders, outfielders, DHs, and two-way players (`TWP`) all stay in. |
| **Pitcher**     | Only `P` (pure pitcher) and `TWP` (two-way players such as Ohtani). Position players are hidden. |

Sometimes a name search has matches but none survive the filter. For
example, you might search `Trout` with *Pitcher* selected and get back
only Mike Trout (CF). In that case the picker shows a hint like
*"No matching pitchers found. Try a different name or switch Position
to Batter."* Flipping the **Position** toggle re-filters the existing
search instantly without re-querying the API.

![The sidebar with Position set to Pitcher. The Metric list switches to ERA / WHIP / K/9 / BB/9 / HR/9. The dropdown filter only admits players whose primary position is P or TWP.](images/sidebar-pitcher-mode.png){width=320px fig-alt="Sidebar in Pitcher mode"}

### Looking up a retiree?

The auto-typeahead window depends on **Player type**:

* **Active players**: covers the current season plus 3 prior seasons.
* **Retired players**: covers ~50 prior seasons (Griffey Jr.,
  Nolan Ryan, Pedro Martínez, etc. all show up).

If a retiree still doesn't appear, click the **Search** button. The
auto window is capped to keep typeahead fast, but the button runs a
deeper lookup (up to ~80 seasons back in Retired mode). That window is
wide enough for mid-century players like Bob Feller or Stan Musial.

::: {.callout-note title="The first typeahead in Retired mode is slow"}
After you switch to *Retired players*, the first name you type pulls
~50 seasonal rosters from the MLB Stats API. On a cold cache that
takes 15–25 seconds; you'll see a top-of-page progress bar while it
runs. Every subsequent keystroke is instant.
:::

## 3. Confirm the pick

After the dropdown fills, pick a row. A small info card appears
underneath with the player's name, primary position, and debut–final
seasons:

![The light-blue card under the picker shows the active selection. It reads SELECTED PLAYER, then the name, then the position and career-year range.](images/selected-player-card.png){width=320px fig-alt="Selected-player info card"}

The card is your last chance to check that the player matches the
**Position** toggle before loading stats. Suppose the card's position
disagrees with the toggle (e.g. you picked a center-fielder while
*Position: Pitcher* is selected). When you click Get Stats, the app
shows a warning notification, and the plot suggests switching the
Position toggle.

## 4. Click Get Stats

Pressing **Get Stats** loads the trajectory plot, the career summary,
and the season log. Picking a name in the dropdown doesn't trigger any
work on its own. That's deliberate: the chart only updates on an
explicit commit, so dropdown re-renders never thrash the display.

## 5. Adjust filters (optional)

* **Min PA / IP per season**: drops noisy partial seasons before the
  curve is fit. Hover the **ⓘ** icon next to the label for the full
  explanation. The default is 100; raise it for true full-time players
  or lower it to include rookie debuts and injury years. See
  [Metrics → Min PA / IP per season](03-metrics.qmd#min-pa-ip-per-season)
  for the threshold reference table.
* **Refresh data cache**: clears the in-process roster and career
  caches. Use it when you've left the app running across a roster
  move or a new MLB game day.

## Reading the chart

* Each dot is one season; dot size scales with playing time (PA
  for batters, IP for pitchers).
* The solid curve is the weighted quadratic fit.
* The shaded ribbon is the 95% confidence band.
* The dashed vertical line marks the fitted peak age. The app only
  draws it when the quadratic is concave-down (i.e. a real peak exists).
* Some pitcher rate metrics are better when lower: **ERA** (earned
  run average), **WHIP** (walks + hits per inning), **BB/9** (walks
  per 9 innings), and **HR/9** (home runs per 9 innings). For these,
  the y-axis is inverted so the peak sits at the top of the chart.

![A batter trajectory. Dot size scales with PA; the curve is the weighted-quadratic fit; the dashed line marks the fitted peak age.](images/career-trajectory-trout.png){width=720px fig-alt="Batter trajectory: Mike Trout's OPS by age"}

![A pitcher trajectory on a lower-is-better metric. Note the inverted y-axis: lower ERA is up, so the fitted peak still visually sits at the top of the chart.](images/career-trajectory-kershaw.png){width=720px fig-alt="Pitcher trajectory: Clayton Kershaw's ERA by age"}

## Reading the Career Summary

The one-row Career Summary table reports:

| Column                   | Meaning                                                           |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Weighted *metric***    | The PA- or IP-weighted career average (rounded to two decimals).  |
| **Total PA / Total IP**  | Lifetime opportunity in the metric's natural unit.                |
| **Best Season**          | The single season with the highest (or for ERA/WHIP, best) value. |
| **Best *metric* / Age**  | Value and the player's age in the best season.                    |
| **Peak Age**             | The age the fitted quadratic peaks at (rounded to two decimals).  |

## Reading the Season Log

The Season Log shows one row per metric, not one row per season.
Each row contains a nanoplot ([great-tables][gt-nanoplot]) that
traces the metric's year-by-year values across the player's career.
Use it to spot rise/peak/decline patterns at a glance without leaving
the page.

![Each metric gets one row with an inline sparkline of year-by-year values. The Metric column spells out the acronym (e.g. "OPS — On-base + Slugging"), so you don't have to scroll back to a legend.](images/season-log-nanoplots.png){width=720px fig-alt="Season Log nanoplots"}

[gt-nanoplot]: https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/reference/GT.fmt_nanoplot.html

## Switching to another player

1. Clear the **Player name** box and type the next name.
2. Pick the new player from the refreshed dropdown.
3. Click **Get Stats** again to commit.

The plot, summary, and season log all update to the newly committed
player. The previous player remains visible until you click Get
Stats, so you can browse search results without losing what you were
looking at.
